5: BULLETIN
6: Hurricane Maria Advisory Number   9
7: NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL152017
8: 1100 AM AST Mon Sep 18 2017
9: 
10: ...MARIA RAPIDLY INTENSIFIES INTO A MAJOR HURRICANE...
11: ...THE EYE IS EXPECTED TO MOVE THROUGH THE LEEWARD ISLANDS LATE THIS
12: AFTERNOON OR THIS EVENING...
13: 
14: 
15: SUMMARY OF 1100 AM AST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
16: -----------------------------------------------
17: LOCATION...14.7N 60.1W
18: ABOUT 60 MI...95 KM E OF MARTINIQUE
19: ABOUT 95 MI...150 KM ESE OF DOMINICA
20: MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...120 MPH...195 KM/H
21: PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
22: MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...959 MB...28.32 INCHES
23: 
24: 
25: WATCHES AND WARNINGS
26: --------------------
27: CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
28: 
29: A Hurricane Warning is now in effect for the U. S. Virgin Islands.
30: 
31: The Meteorological Service of Antigua has issued a Hurricane
32: Warning for the British Virgin Islands, and a Tropical Storm Warning
33: for Anguilla.
34: 
35: SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
36: 
37: A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
38: * Guadeloupe
39: * Dominica
40: * St. Kitts, Nevis, and Montserrat
41: * Martinique
42: * St. Lucia
43: * U.S. Virgin Islands
44: * British Virgin Islands
45: 
46: A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
47: * Antigua and Barbuda
48: * Saba and St. Eustatius
49: * St. Maarten
50: * Anguilla
51: 
52: A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
53: * Puerto Rico, Vieques, and Culebra
54: * Saba and St. Eustatius
55: * St. Maarten
56: * St. Martin and St. Barthelemy
57: * Anguilla
58: 
59: A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
60: * Barbados
61: * St. Vincent and the Grenadines
62: 
63: A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
64: somewhere within the warning area.  Preparations to protect life and
65: property should be rushed to completion.
66: 
67: A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
68: expected somewhere within the warning area.
69: 
70: A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
71: within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
72: before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
73: winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
74: dangerous.
75: 
76: A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
77: possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
78: 
79: Interests elsewhere in the Lesser Antilles and the Dominican
80: Republic should monitor the progress of this system.  Hurricane
81: Warnings will likely be issued for Puerto Rico and the nearby
82: islands this afternoon.
83: 
84: For storm information specific to your area in the United
85: States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
86: monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
87: forecast office. For storm information specific to your area outside
88: the United States, please monitor products issued by your national
89: meteorological service.
90: 
91: 
92: DISCUSSION AND 48-HOUR OUTLOOK
93: ------------------------------
94: At 1100 AM AST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Maria was located
95: near latitude 14.7 North, longitude 60.1 West. Maria is moving
96: toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h), and this motion
97: with some decrease in forward speed is expected through Tuesday
98: night.  On the forecast track, the center of Maria will move across
99: the Leeward Islands late today and tonight, over the extreme
100: northeastern Caribbean Sea Tuesday and Tuesday night, and approach
101: Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands on Wednesday.
102: 
103: Reports from an Air Force Reserve Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicate
104: that maximum sustained winds have increased to near 120 mph
105: (195 km/h) with higher gusts.  Maria is a category 3 hurricane on
106: the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.  Additional rapid
107: strengthening is forecast during the next 48 hours, and Maria is
108: expected to be a dangerous major hurricane as it moves through the
109: Leeward Islands and the northeastern Caribbean Sea.
110: 
111: Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the
112: center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
113: (205 km).
114: 
115: The minimum central pressure estimated from the Hurricane Hunter
116: aircraft data is 959 mb (28.32 inches).
117: 
118: 
119: HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
120: ----------------------
121: WIND:  Hurricane conditions are first expected within portions of
122: the Leeward Islands by late today, with tropical storm conditions
123: beginning during the next few hours.  Hurricane conditions should
124: spread through the remainder of the hurricane warning area tonight
125: through Tuesday night.  Hurricane conditions are possible within the
126: hurricane watch area Tuesday through Wednesday, with tropical
127: storm conditions possible later today or tonight.  Tropical storm
128: conditions are possible in the tropical storm watch area through
129: tonight.
130: 
131: STORM SURGE:  A dangerous storm surge accompanied by large and
132: destructive waves will raise water levels by as much as 6 to 9 feet
133: above normal tide levels in the hurricane warning area near where
134: the center of Maria moves across the Leeward Islands and the
135: British Virgin Islands.
136: 
137: The combination of a dangerous storm surge and the tide will cause
138: normally dry areas near the coast to be flooded by rising waters
139: moving inland from the shoreline.  The water is expected to reach
140: the following heights above ground if the peak surge occurs at the
141: time of high tide...
142: 
143: Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands...6 to 9 ft
144: 
145: The deepest water will occur along the immediate coast near and to
146: the north and east of the landfall location, where the surge will be
147: accompanied by large and destructive waves.  Surge-related
148: flooding depends on the relative timing of the surge and the tidal
149: cycle, and can vary greatly over short distances.  For information
150: specific to your area, please see products issued by your local
151: National Weather Service forecast office.
152: 
153: RAINFALL:  Maria is expected to produce total rain accumulations of
154: 6 to 12 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 20 inches across the
155: central and southern Leeward Islands, and the U.S. and British
156: Virgin Islands through Wednesday night. Rainfall amounts of 6 to 12
157: inches with isolated maximum amounts of 25 inches are expected
158: across Puerto Rico.  Maria is also expected to produce total rain
159: accumulations of 2 to 4 inches with isolated maximum amounts of 8
160: inches over the remaining northern Leeward Islands from Barbuda to
161: Anguilla, eastern portions of the Dominican Republic, as well as the
162: Windward Islands and Barbados. Rainfall on all of these islands
163: could cause life-threatening flash floods and mudslides.
164: 
165: SURF:  Swells generated by Maria are affecting the Lesser Antilles.
166: These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
167: current conditions.  Please consult products from your local
168: weather office.
169: 
170: 
171: NEXT ADVISORY
172: -------------
173: Next intermediate advisory at 200 PM AST.
174: Next complete advisory at 500 PM AST.
175: 
176: $$
177: Forecaster Beven

148: Crystal River FL to Anclote River FL...4-6 ft
149: Anclote River to Anna Maria Island FL including Tampa Bay...2-4 ft

158: conditions expected by tonight or early Wednesday.  Tropical storm

161: storm watch area by that time.  Hurricane conditions are possible
162: within the hurricane watch area by Wednesday.

165: amounts through Friday...

169: and mudslides.

172: Georgia...4 to 8 inches, with isolated maximum amounts of 12 inches.
173: This rainfall could lead to life threatening flash floods.
